## Holds
- Reran the check on branch `cl62` (worktree of origin/cl62): `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_cl62_start_now_stop.py` → 11 of 11 OK.
- Breaks: applied the post's `sed` to `kit/hooks/kit_queue_stop.py` → 1 failure (FAILED, failures=1); restored, tree clean. The check can fail.
- Sampled bar "Split on `_orchestrator`: 2 of 2 cases": broke the read of `split` in `scripts/kit.py` `split_owners` (`get("split")` → `get("splitX")`) → `test_a_split_on_orchestrator_counts_as_held_for_this_one_only` fails; restored. The test asserts both sides (me → S1, other → S2), so "2 of 2" is real.
- The owner's 03:15 ask ("a step-state line under `_orchestrator` is refused when written"), done on the gate itself with the real line and paraphrases (`scripts/review/CR-cl62-the-orchestrator-cannot-end-a-turn-with-paraphrases.py`):
  - refused: "M2 and M3 wait on M1", "M2 waits for CL61 (shares install.py)", "CL61 blocked by CL41";
  - **passes**: "M3 can't start until M1 lands", "M2/M3 depend on M1", "M2 needs M1 first", "Hold M2 until M1 lands", "M2, M3: after M1", "Next: launch M3 once M1 is landed".
  The exact line that misled orchestrator 2 is refused; a reworded one gets through. This is a regex over verbs, so it will always leak; the real protection is the Stop hook (an unlaunched start-now step refuses the stop whatever was written), which holds.
- The owner's 03:18 ask (the three orchestrator guides say no hand-over text, the successor runs resume and nothing else): `test_the_guides_say_resume_and_nothing_else` passes on all three templates.
- Not checked: the full suite (the post claims 81 of 81; `kit.py land` runs the check on main + cl62 together); a live orchestrator turn on the web; the real-project run (post: none; K2 applies, `kit/hooks/*` and `scripts/kit.py` changed).

## Goal
The train `takeover` serves: a successor orchestrator (or a web takeover) continues from the board alone, with nothing to trust but resume. CL62's measure (a Stop refused while a start-now step is neither launched nor held) is the consequence the owner felt (M2/M3 launched 40 minutes late), not a stand-in: good. The owner's own example (02:28: M3 flagged start now after M1 landed 02:18) is a bar and passed on the git copy. Across posts: this is the third rule added to stop an orchestrator writing state it should compute (CL28 fresh resume, M12 hand-over, now CL62); the pattern says "compute, never write", and the gate on free text is the weakest of the three. No sign the owner has tried a takeover himself since; the next real takeover is the try.

## Verdict
continue. The Stop hook does what he asked and can fail; the text gate is partial and should be widened or replaced by "no free text under `_orchestrator` from an orchestrator except what a kit command writes".
